questions.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=12{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t) \\  & =48{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(48{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+1) \\  & =144{t}^{2}-18t\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=\frac{7}{{t}^{3}}+{t}^{2}.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{7}{{t}^{3}}+{t}^{2}) \\  & =-\frac{21}{{t}^{4}}+2t\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{21}{{t}^{4}}+2t) \\  & =\frac{84}{{t}^{5}}+2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The velocity $v$ (in $\text{m/s}$) of a particle at time $t$ (in seconds) is given by $v(t)=(t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+4t).$ Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration $a$ is equal to $6\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+4t) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1+4 \\  & =5+\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the time when the acceleration is $a=6,$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =5+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡t & =1 \\ {e}^{(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)} & ={e}^{1} \\ t & =e\end{aligned}
$$

Then, to calculate the velocity at time $t=e,$ we substitute this into the equation for the velocity:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(e) & =(e\operatorname{ln}⁡e+4e) \\  & =e(1)+4e \\  & =5e\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity when $a=6\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is $5e\text{ m/s}.$
